description: FIRST PATTERN-OF-A-HOLE-FEATURE GOLDEN (FINDINGS #1 — a pattern of the flagship Hole feature silently DUPLICATED THE WHOLE BODY instead of arraying the cut: cut-array inference recognized ONLY extrude-cut, so a Hole source fell through to the whole-body UNION path and the bolt-circle flow through the Hole feature produced a fused pile of plates, not a drilled plate). A 60 x 60 mm square plate sketched on the XY datum, extruded 10 mm into the box [-30,30] x [-30,30] x [0,10]; a SINGLE r4 through-hole drilled by the HOLE FEATURE at (20,0) on the +Z face; then a LINEAR PATTERN along -X (spacing 20 mm, count 3). Because the immediately-preceding body-affecting feature is a Hole, the pattern arrays THAT hole's removal tool (FINDINGS #1 fix): the seed hole is placement 0 and its captured bore tool is REMOVED at placements 1..2 (x = 0, -20), so the result is a ROW of three holes REMOVED, not three bodies added. A four-feature TREE (sketch -> extrude add -> hole -> linear pattern) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as every other golden. Locks: the pattern cut-source inference over a Hole (prev_body_feature is a HoleFeature -> state.last_hole_tools), the exact bore-tool capture at hole-eval time (no post-cut face re-resolution), linear_pattern_cut's translated-tool placement + variadic body.cut + single-solid finalize, GProp over the drilled plate, exact topology after clean(), and (via the parametrized gates) in-process + interpreter-restart byte-determinism and STEP round-trip. The extrude-cut pattern path is UNCHANGED and regression-guarded by pattern-cut-6hole-boltcircle-60x60x10; the whole-body add-pattern by pattern-linear-3x-bar.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Plate: outer square x,y in [-30,30] on XY (4 lines, no constraints -> zero residual, planegcs returns input positions bitwise, same posture as the box/pattern goldens), extruded 10 mm along +Z = the box [-30,30] x [-30,30] x [0,10], volume 60*60*10 = 36000 mm^3.

seed hole: the HOLE feature drills a diameter-8 (r4) through-all bore at (20,0) on the +Z face (outward normal +Z). The drill cuts INTO the solid along -Z, removing exactly pi*4^2*10 per hole. The hole is strictly interior (centre 20 from origin + r4 = max reach 24 < 30 half-width) so it does not touch the plate boundary.

pattern: linear along -X, spacing 20 mm, count 3. The source feature is the Hole, so the pattern REPLICATES THAT HOLE'S removal tool: placement 0 is the seed hole at (20,0); placements 1..2 are the captured bore tool translated -20 and -40 mm in X, i.e. three holes centred at x = 20, 0, -20 (all y=0). Adjacent centres are 20 mm apart, r4 each -> 12 mm clearance, so the three holes are mutually disjoint and each is fully interior (|x|+4 <= 24 < 30); the plate stays one connected solid (a cut that severed it would be pattern_disjoint).
volume = 36000 - 3 * (pi * 4^2) * 10 = 36000 - 480*pi = 34492.0355262769 mm^3 (three disjoint cylindrical through-holes removed, no overlap, so exactly 3x the single-hole removal).

surface_area = 2*(3600 - 3*pi*16)  [top + bottom plate caps, each pierced by all three holes]  + 4*(60*10)  [four outer side walls]  + 3*(2*pi*4*10)  [three cylindrical hole walls]  = 2*3600 - 2*48*pi + 2400 + 3*80*pi = 7200 - 96*pi + 2400 + 240*pi = 9600 + 144*pi = 10052.38934211693 mm^2.

centroid = (0, 0, 5) mm by symmetry: the three hole centres x = 20, 0, -20 are symmetric about x=0, all at y=0, and the holes run the full uniform depth (z mid-height 5). A biased translation error would pull the centroid off (0,0).
bounding_box = [-30,-30,0]..[30,30,10]: the holes are strictly interior, so the AABB is the un-drilled plate's box, unchanged by the cut pattern.

topology: 9 faces (top + bottom plate caps, 4 outer side walls, 3 cylindrical hole walls), 21 edges (top boundary = 4 rect edges + 3 hole circles = 7; bottom = 7; 4 vertical box corner edges; 1 vertical seam edge on each of the 3 periodic hole cylinders = 3), 1 shell. This is the 6-hole bolt-circle golden's structure with 3 fewer cylinder faces and 9 fewer edges (3 fewer hole circles top+bottom + 3 fewer seams), proving the pattern cut ran and clean() collapsed the seams (an unmerged cut or a whole-body union would show a different face/shell count entirely).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default, isRelative=False): each full hole circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments (the same 2x-angular rule the cylinder/6-hole goldens exhibit; radius 4 keeps linear deflection non-binding). Three periodic hole cylinders = 3 * ((126+1)*2 nodes, 126*2 tris) = 3 * (254, 252) = 762 vertices / 756 triangles. Each plate cap is a planar face with a 4-node rectangular outer loop + three 126-gon holes = 4 + 3*126 = 382 boundary nodes, triangulated with holes to 382 - 2 + 2*3 = 386 triangles (no interior node); two caps = 764 vertices / 772 triangles. Four rectangular side walls = 4 * (4 nodes, 2 tris) = 16 vertices / 8 triangles. Totals = 762 + 764 + 16 = 1542 vertices and 756 + 772 + 8 = 1536 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces — same convention as the box/cylinder/6-hole goldens).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-CUT + PURE-TRANSLATION tolerance, measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). Unlike the rotating pattern-cut-6hole golden (60/120/180/240/300 deg trig -> worst residual ~1.46e-11 -> documented 1e-8), this golden only TRANSLATES the cylindrical bore tool (exact placement math, no trig), so the only residual is the curved-wall GProp Gauss quadrature. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-24, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs): volume EXACTLY 0.0, surface_area |10052.38934211693 - 10052.389342116929| ~ 1.1e-12, centroid.x ~ 1.45e-15, centroid.y ~ 8.1e-18, centroid.z / AABB bounds exactly 0.0. Documented ceiling 1e-9 covers the worst measured residual (~1.1e-12, the curved surface_area) with ~860x headroom for libm/BLAS/platform variation across CI hosts, matching the 1e-9 tier of the TRANSLATION pattern goldens (pattern-linear-3x-bar) rather than the looser 1e-8 of the ROTATING curved cut — the placement here is exact, so only the curved GProp (not trig) contributes. It stays 100x tighter than the standing planar 1e-7 kernel bound. Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
